text:
Sam: heads-up, reproduced a stall in staging where prefetch workers + eviction sweeps end up in a circular wait. happening under high demote frequency. stack gist: ```prefetch_worker.lock(shard)
evict_sweep.lock(tenant)
evict_sweep.wait_for(prefetch_release)
prefetch_worker.wait_for(evict_quiesce) // cycle```
Alisha: can you drop the link to the trace?
Sam: pasted in #eng-runtime GIST: https://gist.github.com/xyz123 (stack + minimal repro)
Maria: saw similar in chaos when demote_interval=5s and prefetch_concurrency >= 4. cold requests pile and then nothing progresses.
Ben: sounds like inverted lock ordering (shard vs tenant). do we have a documented lock hierarchy?
Chen: not formally. two quick fixes: 1) flip prefetch to acquire tenant then shard (consistent ordering), or 2) make eviction avoid blocking on prefetch by asking it to hand off.
Sam: flipping ordering is simplest for correctness but could enlarge critical sections for latency-sensitive paths. risk: throughput hit for small RT requests.
Alisha: alternate: eviction does a non-blocking steal RPC to prefetch: `StealPrefix(tenant, prefix)` -> prefetch either yields or returns holder info. avoids lock reorder but adds RPC failure modes.
Ben: steal RPC feels nicer operationally (no global lock changes) but needs idempotent handoff and clear failure/retry semantics. more complex correctness proof.
Kai: I'll run perf matrix comparing: (A) lock-order flip, (B) steal RPC, (C) read-mode tenant lock + exclusive for eviction. use our hotset workload.
Maria: please include demote intervals [2s, 10s, 30s] and prefetch conc 1..8. measure 95/99/prevail stall rate.
Chen: middle-ground design: prefetch acquires tenant lock in shared/read mode, eviction takes exclusive. avoids ordering change and keeps prefetch cheap. downside: need upgrade support (read->write) without deadlock.
Sam: we don't have a safe lock-upgrade primitive; naive upgrade can deadlock when multiple readers try to upgrade. need try_lock+backoff loop or upgrade token coordinator.
Alisha: telemetry idea: sample a small "lock_wait_chain" when a goroutine blocks > 5ms — record which locks held and what it's waiting on. create alert if cycles detected in staging.
Ben: yes. add histograms: `lock_wait_time{lock,role}` and sampled `waiter_chain` strings. low-sample rate to limit overhead.
Sam: short-term mitigation: implement bounded-wait for eviction. if eviction can't acquire prefetch token within X ms, it requeues and increments a backoff counter. reduces chance of global stall while we iterate.
Maria: bounded-wait will slow eviction progress and may increase memory pressure. pair with a temporary tighter eviction budget to avoid OOM.
evict-bot: created INF-2345: "staging: prefetch-evict circular wait" and INF-2346: "telemetry: lock_wait_chain sampling"
Kai: starting runs now. will post CSV of tail latencies and stall counts later today.
Ben: I'll draft a proto for StealPrefix and enumerate failure cases (prefetch crashed, partial handoff, duplicate steals).
Chen: I'll prototype read-mode tenant lock with try_upgrade pattern + backoff. will add unit tests for upgrade races.
Alisha: I'll open a telemetry PR for lock_wait_chain + a staging canary that fails the build if stall_rate > 0.1% over 30m.
Sam: action items recap in one line: 1) Kai perf matrix, 2) Ben steal RPC proto + correctness doc, 3) Chen try-upgrade prototype, 4) Alisha telemetry + canary, 5) short-term bounded-wait patch. meet tomorrow for results.
Maria: +1. also log which tenants were affected in the repro. seems skewed to a few mid-size tenants with hot prefixes.
Ben: note for proto: make StealPrefix idempotent and include holder_generation to detect stale holders. pseudo: ```rpc StealPrefix(tenant, prefix, request_id) returns {status, holder_generation, metadata}``` tag `// handoff must be idempotent`
Chen: on try-upgrade: using try_lock loop with randomized backoff avoids convoying. tests: 1) two readers both try upgrade -> ensure one backs off.
Sam: let's be careful with deploy order for any lock-flip. must deploy prefetch change and then eviction change in two-step canary.
Alisha: also add lint rule reminder: prefix-cache handoffs annotated `// non-blocking handoff required` so code reviews catch blocking changes.
Kai: pinging when bench done. expect initial numbers in ~3h.
Sam: thanks. I'll sketch a short postmortem once we have perf + telemetry.
